title: Evidence-backed comparison of local inference servers
objective:
Research, for a single-machine multi-agent cluster, how SGLang, vLLM and llama.cpp's server compare, focusing on concurrency and queueing, KV/prefix caching, OpenAI tool calling, structured output, cancellation and usage observability, and operational limits. Produce a decision recommendation that cites evidence and a list of questions that still need a local experiment.

Use `web_fetch` on the official documentation and official repositories only: docs.sglang.io, docs.vllm.ai, blog.vllm.ai, and the GitHub repositories of sgl-project/sglang, vllm-project/vllm and ggml-org/llama.cpp. Read at least twelve distinct official pages, at least four per project, and continue by following links you find on those pages. Organise the work with one child management node per engine plus one comparison-and-citation worker; share the evidence table over the blackboard and use cross-subtree messages to resolve contradictions between sources.

Deliverables in {{workspace}}: `report.md`, `sources.json` (one record per fetched page, with source_id, request URL, final URL, fetch time, hash) and `claims.json` (one record per claim, with `{claim, source_ids, quotes, confidence, unverified}`).

initial_transactions.objective: Own the comparison report and the final citation check for the SGLang / vLLM / llama.cpp server comparison in {{workspace}}. Delegate one engine per child management node and add a direct worker that cross-checks claims against the captured sources.
initial_transactions.expected_output: report.md, sources.json and claims.json in {{workspace}}, with every claim pointing at a captured source.
acceptance_criteria: At least twelve distinct official pages were really fetched, at least four per project
Every cited source_id exists and its quoted passage is locatable in the captured text
All six comparison dimensions are covered without silent omissions
Conflicting statements between official versions are preserved as conflicts, not silently resolved
Questions that need a local experiment are listed explicitly
